initial_findings.finding: A process-level NODE_TLS_REJECT_UNAUTHORIZED=0 setting could suppress implicit certificate authorization.
initial_findings.closure: The native claim transport now sets rejectUnauthorized=true explicitly, and a focused mismatch test proves no claim bytes are sent under the hostile setting.

initial_findings.finding: The browser example accepted an unbound raw credential that could be retained and reused across Hub endpoints.
initial_findings.closure: The example now requires an endpoint- and Hub-bound credential envelope, validates both bindings before use, clears the control after valid ingestion, and includes a cross-Hub zero-request regression source.

initial_findings.finding: Native response conversion could throw outside the request promise for null-body or invalid HTTP statuses.
initial_findings.closure: Response conversion is guarded, 204/205/304 use a null body, out-of-range statuses reject through the typed path, and the focused suite covers all cases.

independent_review.delta_check_scope: Read-only recheck of the three closures, direct 205 coverage, and this receipt; unchanged suites were not rerun.
independent_review.chrome_note: The updated cross-Hub browser regression remains added and typechecked but was not run because the shared Chrome lane was held.

canonical_contract.trust_rule: normal CA and hostname verification plus SHA-256 of the connected DER leaf before claim request bytes

compatibility_decision.node: The Node entry point uses a fresh non-pooled HTTPS connection, explicitly requires certificate authorization even if the process disables TLS verification, retains CA and hostname verification, checks the invitation DER leaf SHA-256 in checkServerIdentity, and only then sends the claim body. nodeTls.ca and an explicit caller-owned claimTransport are supported; no global TLS setting is changed.
compatibility_decision.browser: Ordinary browser Fetch cannot inspect the connected certificate. claimPairing now fails with hub_tls_pin_unavailable before discovery or claim I/O unless an embedding supplies a pin-capable claimTransport. Browser reads and rotation retain normal Web PKI; the example requires an endpoint- and Hub-bound caller-owned credential envelope and clears the control after ingestion.
compatibility_decision.api: Existing factories, HubClient methods, credential stores, and Fetch injection remain. The security correction changes previously permissive browser claim behavior to fail closed and adds optional claimTransport and nodeTls inputs plus typed pin errors.
